metadata.sizeJustification: One npm package delivered as one parent work item (PAN-4927 W-INT2): 15 small package files plus one test file per source module (8) and 4 docs/verification files, in 3 subsystems (integrations/openclaw, tests/unit, configuration). Splitting the package across sibling issues would ship a plugin whose manifest contracts.tools cannot match its registrations; the items are already sliced per module so they run in parallel.

narratives.Problem: PAN-4927 FR-15 needs a real, installable OpenClaw plugin so an OpenClaw gateway can see and steer Overdeck through the Overdeck connector or Tailscale. integrations/openclaw/ holds only the shared skill copy today. The parent W-INT2 text was written against the 2026-05 OpenClaw checkout; the current release (2026.10.10) reads only documented manifest keys, keeps entry points in package.json, and its SDK package is 274 MB and needs Node 24.16+.
narratives.Proposal: Build @overdeck/openclaw 0.1.0 as a zero-dependency ESM package: a plain-object plugin entry typed by local structural interfaces (no openclaw import), a manifest with documented keys only and contracts.tools [overdeck_pending, overdeck_answer], a fetch-based JSON-RPC client to the connector (or the dashboard over Tailscale), a 5-minute-throttled before_prompt_build needs-you summary, and two chat tools. overdeck_answer is off unless allowAnswers is true, takes { item, ref, choice }, refuses when the ref no longer matches, and maps each prompt kind to one Overdeck answer tool with named arguments only. The Overdeck MCP tools themselves reach OpenClaw through mcp.servers with transport streamable-http; the README carries the exact openclawConfig snippets. CP-7 is answered from the 2026.10.10 docs and confirmed live with openclaw plugins validate / mcp probe / plugins inspect under Node 24.17 against the dashboard /mcp, recorded in docs/verification.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Publishing the package to npm, ClawHub or any catalog (PAN-4927 D-5).
- The CI job that builds and tests this package (W-CI1).
- configuration/bots.mdx and the other W-DOC pages.
- Native proxy tools for every Overdeck tool (the CP-7(a) fallback); only a follow-up issue if CP-7(a) fails.
- Manifest mcpServers, OpenClaw MCP OAuth (auth: "oauth"), and public /mcp for OpenClaw.
- Editing integrations/shared/SKILL.md or any skill copy.
- Any change to Overdeck server code, botSnippets.ts or the connector.
- Answering multi-question prompts through overdeck_answer (D-7).
- Reporting list_pending_input fleetError in overdeck_pending or the summary.
- A runtime or development dependency on the openclaw package.

autoDecisions.summary: Export a plain plugin-definition object typed by local interfaces instead of importing definePluginEntry (changes parent D-22 wording).
autoDecisions.rationale: definePluginEntry in openclaw 2026.10.10 is a pure builder of the same object; importing it needs the 274 MB openclaw package with Node >=24.16 in a Node 22 repo, and local-path installs would not resolve it. The MYN model ships this shape in production; the live CP-7 check runs the real host.

autoDecisions.summary: Manifest uses documented keys only; drop the parent draft's entry and license keys; the entry is package.json openclaw.extensions.
autoDecisions.rationale: OpenClaw 2026.10.10 docs: only documented manifest fields are read; entry points and compat live in package.json#openclaw.

autoDecisions.summary: Compatibility floor >=2026.5.6 in openclaw.compat.pluginApi, openclaw.install.minHostVersion and an optional peer dependency.
autoDecisions.rationale: Only 2026.5.6 (local checkout) and 2026.10.10 were checked; an optional peer keeps npm ci from installing the host.

autoDecisions.summary: configSchema does not mark localToken required; the tools answer a setup error instead.
autoDecisions.rationale: plugins install enables the plugin by default, and a required field missing from config would invalidate the whole OpenClaw config.

autoDecisions.summary: register always registers both contracted tools; a bad URL or missing token becomes the tools' answer text.
overdeck_answer takes { item, ref, choice } with an 8-hex ref and refuses when the ref no longer matches item.
autoDecisions.rationale: The pending list can change between listing and answering; without the check an item number could answer a different prompt.

autoDecisions.summary: overdeck_answer answers single-question prompts only; multi-question prompts point at overdeck__answer_question or the dashboard.
autoDecisions.rationale: One choice string cannot carry several answers without a separator free text could contain.

autoDecisions.summary: Summary fetches at most once per 5 minutes per gateway and injects only on the fetching turn.
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids repeating the same context every turn and bounds connector load.

autoDecisions.summary: CP-7 runs live against the dashboard's own /mcp with a short-lived read-only token, not through a paired connector.
autoDecisions.rationale: The dashboard /mcp uses the same sessionless JSON Streamable HTTP as the connector; a connector pairing needs the operator's overdeck.ai sign-in.

autoDecisions.summary: If CP-7(a) fails, record it, file a follow-up issue for native proxy tools and tell the orchestrator instead of building the fallback here.
autoDecisions.rationale: The 2026.10.10 docs state embedded OpenClaw exposes mcp.servers tools, so the fallback is unlikely and large.

autoDecisions.summary: Behavior tests live in the package; a root tests/unit/integrations/openclaw.test.ts covers package shape so CI checks it before W-CI1 exists.
autoDecisions.rationale: Root vitest does not include integrations/; grok-bot set the same precedent.

JSON-RPC tools/call client over fetch (mcp-client.ts)

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3. createMcpClient({ url, token, fetch? }) returns callTool(name, args, { timeoutMs? }). One POST to url.href with content-type application/json, accept "application/json, text/event-stream" (the SDK transport answers 406 without text/event-stream) and authorization Bearer <token>; body { jsonrpc: "2.0", id: counter, method: "tools/call", params: { name, arguments: args } }. Timeout 10 s default via AbortController + setTimeout cleared in finally (never AbortSignal.timeout). Throw OverdeckMcpError with exactly the WI-3 step 4 messages; messages name at most url.origin and never the token. Build the test token at runtime as ['odl', 'a'.repeat(64)].join('_') so no token-shaped literal is committed (WI-10 scan, GitHub push protection). Success returns { isError: result.isError === true, text: joined text blocks }.

items.title: callTool sends one POST whose headers include accept "application/json, text/event-stream" and authorization "Bearer <token>" and whose body is a JSON-RPC tools/call with the given name and arguments

Given HTTP 401, HTTP 500, a fetch rejection, a JSON-RPC error, a non-JSON body and a 10 s timeout on fake timers, callTool throws OverdeckMcpError with the WI-3 messages and none contains the token string
A result with two text blocks returns their texts joined by a newline, and result.isError true returns isError true

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5 (the full rules are there; follow them literally). parsePendingInput(text) flattens list_pending_input JSON in order: machines, then each machine's conversations (surfaces in order permission, ask, plan, pane choice, held kickoff), then its agents (ask, each permission request, exitPlanMode, other kinds). Kind by harness: codex-approval when toolUseId starts with "codex-approval:" or harness codex; pi-ask for ohmypi or pi; question for claude-code; dashboard-only otherwise. Single-question rule (D-7). Remote agents (remote true or id starting with "@") are not answerable. ref = first 8 hex of sha256(JSON.stringify([kind, targetKey, refKey])). formatPendingList and summaryText produce exactly the WI-5 step 6-7 texts, collapse whitespace with oneLine, cap summary at 5 items of 300 characters. Non-JSON or missing machines throws "list_pending_input returned an unexpected answer". Build the fixture covering every branch listed in WI-5 with invented values only.

items.title: Given tests/fixtures/pending-input.json, parsePendingInput returns items whose kinds appear in the exact WI-5 order, and linked conversation names keep their "@env-1/" prefix
Each item ref is 8 lowercase hex characters, equal across two parses, and different when only the item signature changes
parsePendingInput returns answerable false with the WI-5 reason for the two-question ask, the opencode ask, the held kickoff and the remote agent items
summaryText returns null for an empty list and otherwise at most 5 item lines of at most 302 characters plus an "and N more" line, and a prompt containing blank lines comes out on one line
parsePendingInput throws "list_pending_input returned an unexpected answer" for text that is not JSON

narrative.Action: PRD WI-6. planAnswer(item, choice) returns { ok, tool, arguments, done } or { ok: false, error }. Trim the choice; refuse empty, longer than 2000 characters, or an item that is not answerable (error = item.reason). resolveOption: option number, then case-insensitive label, then free text. Map each kind to the exact tool and argument object in the WI-6 table (answer_permission, answer_question, answer_pi_ask, answer_codex_approval, answer_plan, answer_pane_choice with selectedIndex = index of the matching option number, answer_agent_permission, answer_agent_plan). Arguments are object literals built from named PendingItem fields only (security review W2). done text as in WI-6 step 5.

items.title: For each of the 9 kinds in the WI-6 table, planAnswer returns that row's tool and an arguments object that toEqual-matches the row exactly
A permission item accepts "Allow-Once" as allow-once, and refuses "allow" with "choice must be one of: allow-once, allow-always, deny"

A pane-choice item with option numbers [1, 2] maps "2" to selectedIndex 1 and refuses "9"; a plan item maps "reject-feedback: shorter" to action reject-feedback with feedback "shorter" and refuses "reject-feedback:" with no text
A question item resolves "1" to the first option label, "YES" to the label "Yes", and other text to that text unchanged

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7. Export TOOL_NAMES ["overdeck_pending", "overdeck_answer"] and createTools({ getConfig, client, setupError }). Tools never throw; they return text. overdeck_pending: list_pending_input -> formatPendingList(parsePendingInput(text)). overdeck_answer steps in WI-7 step 4 order: (1) getConfig().allowAnswers false -> refusal with zero client calls; (2) client null -> setup text; (3) read only item, ref, choice and validate them; (4) list again and refuse unless items[item-1].ref === ref; (5) planAnswer; (6) callTool(plan.tool, plan.arguments) and return plan.done. Test tokens are built at runtime as in mcp-client, never as one literal. Map "Unknown tool list_pending_input" and "Unknown tool answer_*" to the read-access and approve-access texts in WI-7 step 2.

items.title: Given allowAnswers false, overdeck_answer returns the "Answering Overdeck prompts from OpenClaw is off" text and the fake client records zero calls

Given params with extra fields conversation "other" and signature "forged", a permission answer sends answer_permission with exactly the conversation, signature and choice taken from the listed item

CP-7 live check against OpenClaw 2026.10.10 and docs/verification.md

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Runs after entry and readme; it edits README.md only when a CP-7 check finds a renamed key, and no later item touches README.md.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-12, steps 1-10, exactly. Build the package on Node 22. In a shell with PATH prefixed by /home/eltmon/.config/nvm/versions/node/v24.17.0/bin, install openclaw@2026.10.10 into $HOME/.overdeck/tmp/pan-4954-cp7/host and isolate it with OPENCLAW_HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH under that directory (never /tmp, never the repo). Run `openclaw plugins validate --root <abs integrations/openclaw> --entry ./dist/index.js` (b). Mint a read-only token with `pan token create cp7-openclaw-probe --scopes read:state,read:conversations --json`, keep it only in OVERDECK_CP7_TOKEN, write the WI-12 step 5 config pointing mcp.servers.overdeck and the plugin at http://127.0.0.1:3011/mcp, run `openclaw mcp probe overdeck --json` (a) and `openclaw plugins inspect overdeck --runtime --json` (b, c). If plugins.load.paths stops on a trust or capability-consent prompt, use `openclaw plugins install <abs integrations/openclaw> --accept-capabilities` instead (WI-12 step 7a). Revoke the token with `pan token revoke <id>`. Write docs/verification.md in the WI-12 step 10 format. If a check fails because of OpenClaw, follow the WI-12 checkpoint: renamed keys -> fix manifest/README and record; (a) failure -> record the error, create the follow-up GitHub issue for native proxy tools, and pan tell flywheel-orchestrator; do not build the proxies here.

items.title: integrations/openclaw/docs/verification.md contains one table row each for CP-7(a), CP-7(b) and CP-7(c) naming OpenClaw 2026.10.10, the command run and its result

When the probe passes, the CP-7(a) row records that `openclaw mcp probe overdeck` listed list_conversations and list_pending_input over streamable-http; when OpenClaw fails it, the row records the error and a follow-up issue link; when the host cannot run it, the row records Not run with the exact message
After the check, `pan token list` shows no active token named cp7-openclaw-probe, and verification.md contains no od[klr]_ token literal
